title: Continuity Ceiling Where Prior-Carrier Claims Are Received and Fills Reach the Limit
content:
The continuity ceiling on a continuity-of-care quantity limit authorization for an acute migraine drug under the Utilization Management Program is the drug's limit times a share of the package's maximum exception multiple, set as follows:

- the whole of the package's maximum exception multiple when **the prior carrier's claims history for the drug has been received on the member's case** and **the member's paid retail fills of the drug reached the limit both in the last month and in the month before it**;
- seven eighths (0.875) of it when exactly one of those two holds;
- a member with neither takes no change under this rule.

**Prior-carrier claims history received** means the member's case history shows clinical information received for the drug on the ground of the prior carrier's approval.

**Fills at the limit.** The paid retail fills are those under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. The months end on the grant date; the last month is the fills dated after the same day of the month one month before the grant date, and the month before it is the fills dated within the last two months but not the last month. A month reaches the limit when its fills of the drug add up to at least the drug's limit: 9 units for sumatriptan, 8 for Nurtec ODT, 16 for Ubrelvy.

## Truth table

| Prior-carrier claims history received | Limit reached in both months | Share of the maximum exception multiple |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | whole |
| Yes | No | seven eighths |
| No | Yes | seven eighths |
| No | No | no change under this rule |

## Figures (hypothetical: Nurtec ODT, limit 8)

| Package maximum exception multiple | Whole: 8 times the multiple | Seven eighths: 8 times seven eighths of the multiple |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 16 | 14 |
| 1.5 | 12 | 10.5 |
